text:
marta: Kicking off a follow-up on the rollout-metadata RFC — thinking about adding an 'annotation expression' primitive so we can target model variants with logical predicates.

marta: Rough example idea:

```
"annotations": {
  "selector_expr": "env == 'prod' && (region == 'us-east' || perf_tier >= 2)",
  "sparse_tags": ["latency-sensitive"],
  "policy_level": "advisory"
}
```

marta: Main concerns: parsing/execution cost, safety (no arbitrary eval), storage compactness, and how older clients should fall back.

vikram: Parser + evaluator are doable but we should define a minimal, safe expression language (no function calls, no arbitrary JSON paths). boolean operators, comparisons, IN, and parentheses should be enough. Perf: compile to a small bytecode and cache compiled forms at the resolver.

vikram: For storage, avoid shipping raw strings in hot manifests — precompute a compact tokenized serialization (array of op-codes) for fast in-memory evaluation.

zack: +1 on tokenized form. Also think about indexing: we need sparse_tags so DB lookups can short-circuit a lot of requests without evaluating heavy expressions per request.

sofia: Telemetry note — if we introduce expressions we should emit which clause matched (match_reason) so we can detect drift and bad coverage. Suggest: resolver emits a one-token match_reason and we sample full expression traces for a small percent of requests.

lisa: From product: we must not expose raw selector_expr to non-tech PMs in the console. Propose two editor modes: visual tag/field builder (default) and an "advanced" text mode for power users.

marta: Fallback semantics brainstorming: Plan A: clients that don't understand selector_expr ignore it and rely on advisory sparse_tags. Plan B: server materializes expressions to explicit tag sets per model/version and ships the materialized set for backward compatibility. Which is safer?

vikram: Plan B is safer operationally — server-side materializer can pre-resolve expressions into concrete selectors and include a compatibility blob. We should also ship a small resolver library for dedicated/private customers to run locally. Add a compatibility flag on manifests so clients know which path was used.

zack: Security: grammar must forbid regex, code execution, and network lookups. Only allow comparisons to constants and enum-like fields.

schema-validator-bot: PR #4821 — rollout-manifest.json failed schema: field 'selector_expr' must be a string matching ^[A-Za-z0-9 _()'\"=<>!&|,-]+$ — see inline comment for allowed chars.

marta: Ok, we'll tighten the grammar and relax the validator once we land a formal grammar. Next steps I propose:
1) Draft minimal expression grammar and a compact serialization (token array).
2) Prototype server-side materializer that outputs per-version materialized tags.
3) Define telemetry match_reason codes and sampling strategy.
4) Console UX sketch: visual builder + advanced mode.

lisa: I’ll own the UX sketch.
sofia: vikram and I will pair on telemetry + resolver perf tests.
zack: marta and I will prototype the materializer and tokenized serializer.

sofia: Ops question — can we rate-limit evaluation error logs? don’t want noisy SLO pages from bad expressions in canaries.

vikram: Yes — sample 1% by default for evaluation errors, with an option to increase sampling for canary manifests.

marta: Thanks all. I created INF-2943 to track work items and will drop a short RFC update tomorrow with the grammar sketch. :white_check_mark:
